hazard: Delay in initiating Mental Health Act assessment

reports.title: Sandra Bodrozic
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: the Clinical Director for the Acute Division has clarified and disseminate the Trust's bed management policy to its employees emphasising that, 'any patient requiring a bed will be offered admission regardless of their Mental Health Act status'
promises.summary: Clarify and disseminate bed management policy to ensure private beds are offered promptly

concerns.quote: no bed was found for her until 30 May, by which time she had changed her mind
the psychiatrist was going on holiday the following day and so decided to leave this until her return, rather than asking colleagues
concerns.hazard: delay in initiating Mental Health Act assessment

concerns.quote: it took until the following week for this to be arranged, and Ms Bodrožic' had killed herself in the meantime
Mental Health Act assessments are, by their very nature, urgent, yet there seemed to be a general acceptance by the team that they will usually take several days to take place
concerns.hazard: lack of urgency in assessment scheduling

concerns.quote: The approved mental health professional (AMHP), a social worker, who visited Ms Bodrožic' on Wednesday, 25 June 2014, decided that she needed a Mental Health Act assessment and immediately made the appropriate referral.
Ms Bodrožic's family were not told that, realistically, they could only obtain an immediate assessment by attending a hospital emergency unit
concerns.hazard: lack of information to family about assessment access

reports.title: Thiago Araujo
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths
Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: Any service user of the Crisis Team who is being considered for discharge because of non-engagement must be discussed in the Crisis Service Multi- Disciplinary Meeting with senior overview of the decision to discharge.
promises.summary: Require crisis team discharge decisions to be reviewed in multidisciplinary meetings and documented

concerns.quote: On 24 January 2020 Mr Araujo had discharged himself from psychiatric inpatient care he was to be supervised by the Camden and Islington NHS trust crisis team. Mr Araujo failed to engage with the crisis team and following a meeting on 30 January 2020 the crisis team closed Mr [name redacted] referral. In the course of this closure no arrangements were made to address the risks presented by Mr Araujo.
concerns.hazard: lack of supervision of discharged psychiatric patient

concerns.quote: Family and carers of patients diagnosed with emotionally unstable personality disorder do not receive support or education upon management of this diagnosis from Camden and Islington NHS Trust, unless the patient has been received for treatment by the personality disorder service.
concerns.hazard: lack of support for families of emotionally unstable personality disorder patients

concerns.quote: By 4 February 2020 the Camden and Islington community recovery team identified an acute risk of suicide in Mr Araujo, faced with his non-compliance with community treatment they considered an admission into inpatient care. No actions were taken to affect this plan.
concerns.hazard: failure to act on acute suicide risk

concerns.quote: In evidence the community recovery team indicated that a factor in their inaction was the knowledge that arranging a section 135 mental health act 1983 warrant and assessment would take two weeks. Such an assessment requires actions by an approved mental health practitioner from the local authority, two section 12 mental health act approved doctors, the assistance of the Metropolitan police and the local magistrates court to secure a warrant. A delay of 14 days in securing a mental health act assessment
concerns.hazard: excessive delay in mental health act assessment

concerns.quote: In the days leading to Mr [name redacted] death his family became aware that he had made an online purchase of which was to be delivered to his father's home. Despite raising these issues with Camden and Islington NHS trust, the Metropolitan police and employees of the post office there appeared to be no process available to the family to escalate their concerns to prevent delivery of this package.
concerns.hazard: inability to prevent delivery of harmful online purchase

links.explanation: Both reports highlight delays in obtaining a Mental Health Act assessment due to a lack of urgency and clear timelines. The earlier report notes a general acceptance of multi‑day waits, while the later report describes a known two‑week delay for section 135 warrants.
